name: Vodafone Idea Ltd
title: Vodafone Idea Ltd - 532822 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Vi's Q4 FY26 is a capex-led recovery story, but the headline profit is an AGR one-off (Rs 55,622 Cr exceptional gain); cash EBITDA grew only 4.8% and FY26 cash EBITDA was flat at Rs 9,217 Cr.

summary.headline: Vodafone Idea booked a Rs 55,622 Cr AGR-related exceptional gain, lifting Q4 FY26 net profit to Rs 51,970 Cr, while Q4 revenue grew 2.9% YoY to Rs 11,332 Cr.
summary.overview: Vodafone Idea reported Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 11,332 Cr (+2.9% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs 4,889 Cr (43.1% margin, +80 bps), with cash EBITDA of Rs 2,432 Cr (+4.8%). The headline profit reflects a one-time exceptional credit of Rs 55,622 Cr from the DoT AGR reassessment, which set dues at Rs 64,046 Cr versus the earlier frozen Rs 87,695 Cr. Operating KPIs improved: subscriber base stabilised at 192.8 Mn, customer ARPU rose 8.3% YoY to Rs 190, and 4G/5G mix reached 66.9%. Management reaffirmed a Rs 45,000 Cr three-year capex plan, which remains contingent on a pending SBI-led debt raise.

segments.name: Consumer mobile
segments.commentary: ARPU rose to Rs 190 on premiumisation and Non-stop Hero unlimited data plan, which grew over 25% QoQ for three quarters. Churn is around 4%, above peers per management.

segments.name: Enterprise
segments.commentary: Momentum cited across connectivity, cloud, IoT, business communications, mobility and cybersecurity in BFSI, manufacturing, utilities, logistics and government. About 1.3 Tbps added in fixed-line capacity across data centres for the 'Dedicated Enterprise Corridor'. No revenue split disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Three-year capex plan of Rs 45,000 Cr remains intact; management expects a 'far greater intensity' of capex from Q1 FY27.
Funding: Rs 25,000 Cr funded facility and Rs 10,000 Cr non-funded facility sought from an SBI-led consortium; no timeline given until closure.
Management targets sustained net customer additions, double-digit revenue growth and 3x EBITDA over three years; cash EBITDA margin ambition above 35% within 3-4 years (currently ~20%).
Management expects some cash-cost inflation going forward as the network-efficiency benefit is lapped, while still offsetting rollout costs.
Targets churn reduction of 0.5%-0.6%; plans 60,000-70,000 additional 4G sites over the next 1-1.5 years covering about 125 Mn population.
Tejas Mehta outlined spectrum payments of Rs 7,000 Cr, Rs 15,000 Cr and Rs 27,000 Cr over FY27-FY29, with no change to the spectrum payout currently being sought.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was Rs 8,742 Cr versus Rs 9,600 Cr in FY25; the three-year plan is Rs 45,000 Cr.
Over the last six quarters, Rs 16,000 Cr deployed; about 30,000 unique broadband towers added (17,300 in FY26) and over 126,000 broadband layers added.
4G capacity expanded by over 27%; 4G population coverage above 86% pan-India.
5G services live in over 80 cities across all 17 circles with 5G spectrum; FWA being piloted on a select basis, with mobility the focus.
Management cited about 48 Mn added population from network expansion in recent quarters; 125 Mn incremental population covered in the last six quarters.
demand_pricing: Customer ARPU Rs 190 in Q4 FY26, up 8.3% YoY; management attributes it to premiumisation, data usage growth and Non-stop Hero.
Data usage per 4G/5G subscriber rose 27.2% YoY to 20.2 GB in Q4 FY26.
Gross adds were about 19.1 Mn in Q4, versus 21.8 Mn in Q2 and 19.3 Mn in Q3, reflecting a deliberate focus on lower-cost, higher-quality acquisition.
Vi holds about 20% share of MNP gains, versus 47% of industry acquisitions coming through porting; 33% of the base still on feature phones.
Smartphone sales dipped recently (management cites RAM-driven price rises), but feature-to-smartphone upgrades run at 3-4% within the network.
Vi's VLR ratio averages 87-88%, with some circles above 92-93% and some near 80%.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the strong sequential ARPU growth, and how much headroom remains versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited data usage growth of over 30%, Non-stop Hero (over 25% QoQ), and network additions. Levers include upgrading the 33% feature-phone base, converting smartphone users not on data, and moving 1.5-2 GB daily quota users to unlimited plans.

qa_highlights.question: Network opex fell sequentially despite site additions; is this sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Network cost was Rs 2,345 Cr versus Rs 2,361 Cr QoQ, helped by diesel reduction, electrification and self-optimised network. Management said cash-cost inflation will likely return as the efficiency benefit is lapped.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the debt raise and promoter shareholding after warrant and CLAM conversions?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt: SBI-led consortium is working on Rs 25,000 Cr funded and Rs 10,000 Cr non-funded facilities; no timeline given. Current holdings are Vodafone plc 16.07% and ABG 9.57%, which will change after conversions. No Board structure change expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why is churn elevated and how will customer additions improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Churn is about 4%, above industry; management is targeting a 0.5-0.6 pp cut as network investment arrests churn. Gross adds were held deliberately lower for better quality.

qa_highlights.question: How does management plan to reach a higher cash EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for double-digit revenue growth and cash EBITDA margin above 35% in three to four years, from about 20.5% now. Levers are ARPU, industry pricing and lower churn in newly-built circles.

qa_highlights.question: How will spectrum payouts from FY28 be funded without further equity?
qa_highlights.answer: Tejas Mehta laid out Rs 105,000 Cr of sources over FY27-FY29 (cash EBITDA ~Rs 60,000 Cr, Rs 25,000 Cr funded debt plus rolling LC ~Rs 35,000 Cr, CLAM and tax refunds ~Rs 10,000 Cr), against uses of about Rs 100,000 Cr. Promoter infusion is additional.

risks_watch: Profit is inflated by the non-recurring Rs 55,622 Cr AGR gain; underlying operating profit is roughly Rs 4,889 Cr per quarter.
Funding of the Rs 45,000 Cr capex plan depends on the SBI-led debt facility, which has no closure timeline.
Spectrum payments of Rs 27,000 Cr are scheduled in FY29, and FY28 onwards depends on cash flows and future funding.
Cash EBITDA was flat YoY at Rs 9,217 Cr, and management expects cost inflation as efficiency gains are lapped.
Churn of about 4% and a 19.1 Mn gross-add run-rate; subscriber growth depends on whether Feb-Mar 2026 net adds continue.
Smartphone market softness from component cost inflation could slow premiumisation.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the AGR resolution, promoter support and the subscriber turn, with heavy reliance on forward targets. Management was less specific on funding timing, circle-level and KPI numbers, and the EBITDA margin path, deferring these to closure or to later years.
key_quotes: We are deeply grateful to the Government of India for conclusively resolving the AGR matter.
So, you will see a far greater intensity of capex starting from quarter 1 and further intensifying in subsequent quarters of this financial year.
We don't want to put a timeline, unless and until its closed.
Our churn is approximately 4%, which is significantly higher than the other operators.

growth.why: Management targets double-digit revenue growth and 3x EBITDA over three years, backed by 60,000-70,000 planned 4G sites and a Rs 45,000 Cr capex plan, but the capex is contingent on an unclosed SBI-led debt raise with no timeline and Q4 revenue grew only 2.9% YoY.
